messages:
jamie: heads up — we've got intermittent DNS failures from a subset of GPU edge nodes this morning. model-fetch pods fail with 'dial tcp: lookup model-registry.internal on 127.0.0.53:53: no such host'. only happens on nodes that just recovered from preemptible interruption.

omar: seen similar. symptoms? stale A records or NXDOMAIN?

jamie: mostly NXDOMAIN but sometimes it resolves to an old internal IP that no longer has the service. looks like resolver cache is returning outdated answers.

sophia: could be a node-local DNS cache that didn't clear after the node got a new egress IP. which resolver stack: systemd-resolved or glue resolver?

jamie: nodes use systemd-resolved with a local stub at 127.0.0.53 -> node-local-dns (k8s DaemonSet) forwards to our edge recursive. I've pasted a failing dig from one of the nodes: 

-----
$ dig +short @127.0.0.53 model-registry.internal
# (on affected node) -> returns 10.11.5.42 (old pod IP)
$ dig +nocmd model-registry.internal @10.2.8.3 +noall +answer
model-registry.internal. 30 IN A 10.2.8.78
-----

jamie: notice TTL mismatch: node-local returned 3600s cached value, recursive returns 30s. cache drift.

lee: that TTL mismatch is nasty. probably our node-local TTL override is not honoring the upstream TTL. or we have duplicate caches in the path (systemd-resolved -> nodelocal -> edge-recursive) and one is slow to evict.

omar: quick checks: 1) cat /etc/resolv.conf on the node to see resolver order; 2) check nodelocal logs for cache evictions; 3) run tcpdump to see if queries go to the expected recursive.

jamie: resolv.conf shows 'nameserver 127.0.0.53' then search includes .internal. ndots is default. nodelocal logs show no eviction entries for those names.

lee: could be a split-horizon or egress-affinity issue where different egress IPs get different answers (upstream backend has per-subnet routing). If a node reboots and now hits a different recursive with stale DB, we get inconsistent views.

omar: also check for negative caching / SOA TTLs. if the recursive incorrectly set negative TTLs or we have a stale negative cache, NXDOMAIN can persist longer.

jamie: good point — capture of full dig +trace shows the authoritative has the current record with low TTL. The recursive cluster that some nodes hit is behind a lagging sync job (we've seen replication lag earlier).

lee: mitigation: for now set node-local-dns to honor upstream TTLs and reduce its max-cache TTL to 60s for the internal zone. push a hotfix config. can someone craft the kube patch?

omar: I'll open a PR to nodelocal configmap to set max-cache-ttl: 60 and enable "respect_upstream_ttl: true" (if supported by our image).

jamie: thanks. also rolling restart for affected nodes after patch. schedule canary on 2 nodes then scale.

infra-bot: deploybot created change-request #2314: nodelocal-configmap update -> set max-cache-ttl=60. CI: helm-lint passed.

lee: after that, we should audit our recursive cluster replication lag and add read-after-write checks post node-recovery to avoid stale reads. can we add a kube-probe that queries the registry and validates canonical IP against the authoritative?

jamie: yes let's add a lightweight probe (curl/dig) in the node-init that checks resolver view and logs divergence. will follow up with a runbook entry.

sophia: also add alert on TTL mismatch between node-local and upstream for internal zones. low noise: only alert if mismatch > 120s and >5% of queries failing.

omar: PR linked here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/nodelocal-dns/pull/42 (contains config diff and rollout steps).

jamie: rolling patch started on two canary nodes. will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:

(12:01) jamie: canary nodes now showing correct answers and TTL 30s from node-local same as upstream. initial model-fetch successes.

(12:10) jamie: rolled to remaining 18 edge nodes in the pool. tracking for 30m.

(12:35) lee: follow-up actions: 1) permanent config change to respect upstream TTL 2) root-cause ticket to fix recursive replica lag 3) add post-recovery resolver check 4) runbook update. I'll create the tickets.

(12:40) jamie: thanks all — incident resolved for now.
